name: Josie Beverages
early_stage_explanation: The evidence supports the early-stage claim. The energy drink line launched in January 2026 through a press release, which is recent. It is sold mainly online (DrinkJosie.com, Amazon, TikTok Shop), with only a few specialty retailers in the SF Bay Area. The site says "Retail locations coming soon," so the footprint is small and not national retail. LinkedIn shows only 70 followers, and there is no sign of a parent company. No priced VC round turned up. The Tracxn and PitchBook hits are for a different company, a Stockholm HR-tech startup also called Josie, so they do not apply. The RM Beverages result is also unrelated. The agent's "traction=none recorded" is thin, but it does not change the early-stage verdict.

name: Ayn Skin House
early_stage_explanation: The evidence supports the agent's claim. Formes de Luxe says Ayn Skin House, founded by Inam Fraihat, launched in July 2025 with five products (exfoliating glove, olive soap, multi-oil body serum, etc.) and two more in development. That is well within the last 2 years. The brand's own site shows a small DTC-style catalog (soap, body oil, kessa glove, rosewater) with no sign of national retail or a parent company. It was a finalist in a Beauty Tank award for newly launched indie brands. No funding evidence turned up: the Tracxn, Companies House and OneSkin results are about unrelated entities (Ayn Enterprises, Ayn Retail Ltd, OneSkin) and don't bear on this company. Nothing suggests a priced VC round, so it looks like a very early, likely bootstrapped brand.
founders_supported_explanation: The cited Formes de Luxe article says "Ayn Skin House founded by Inam Fraihat", which shows Inam Fraihat as the founder of Ayn Skin House. The claim gives the role "Founder" and no background, so there are no further details to check. No claims failed.

name: Sainte Labs
early_stage_explanation: The evidence supports the agent's claim. Sainte Labs soft-launched on October 12, 2025, and the Formes de Luxe article confirms an October 2025 launch, so the brand is under a year old. The company is an LLC founded by two makeup artists, and no source shows it is owned by a larger company. It sells primarily DTC, with a few best-selling SKUs on Amazon, so its footprint is small and not national retail. About eight SKUs are still in development. The Beauty Tank award is real, and it was won in a competition for newly launched indie brands. The independent search found nothing on funding; the Isigny Sainte, Sente, Sainte Anne and Sentient Labs results are all about different companies. No priced VC round is evidenced, and the absence of funding news fits a bootstrapped or pre-seed company.
founders_supported_explanation: Both founders are shown as founders of Sainte Labs, but some background details are not in the sources provided. Beth Bender: the Digital Heroes page lists her as Co-Founder who runs Sainte Labs in Los Angeles, and PRLog says she is a beauty industry veteran who created the brand. That supports the role, the Los Angeles location and the veteran description. Not shown: that she is a make-up artist, and the October 2025 launch date. The PRLog text mentions professional artistry only at brand level, and the Forbes Deluxe (formesdeluxe) page was not provided, so it cannot be checked. Lia Robins: PRLog says the brand was created by beauty industry veterans Beth Bender and 'Lia Robin' (spelled without the s), and that it came from their firsthand frustration with products. That supports co-founder status, the veteran description and the frustration story. Failed detail: the make-up artist description is not explicitly attributed to her in the available sources. There is also a minor name spelling discrepancy (Robin vs Robins). The 'Co-Founder' title for Lia is implied by 'created by' rather than stated. Overall, the founders are supported, but the make-up artist and October 2025 launch details are unverified.

name: LĪNA (Lina Universal Balm)
early_stage_explanation: The evidence supports the early-stage claim. The brand launched in June 2025 (Formes de Luxe; the press release is dated May 2025) with a single product, the Universal Balm, which is made in LA. It sells online DTC, with a spa and private-club rollout only planned. The founder is a solo makeup artist, and the entity is The LINA Group LLC. Coverage is small: local LA press, a PRNewswire release and PRLog, plus a Beauty Tank finalist spot and an award nomination. No priced VC round or outside funding appears anywhere. The Tracxn results are for unrelated companies (Lina Stores, LiNa Energy). There is no sign of a parent company or national retail distribution.
founders_supported_explanation: Both people are shown as founders. Lina Leikam is called Founder in The Fox Magazine and the press releases. Thomas Leikam is listed as Co-Founder under Leadership on the LinkedIn company page. Most of Lina's background is backed by the Voyage LA interview: she is from Germany, graduated from barber school, worked as a hairdresser in Berlin, earned the Beni Durrer Hair & Makeup Artistry diploma, and has over 13 years across film, TV, editorial and commercial work. The Fox Magazine confirms she is Los Angeles-based. The failed claim is the 'Esthetician' title, which none of the cited pages mention. They describe her only as a makeup artist, so that part of the background is unsupported.

name: todo
early_stage_explanation: The evidence supports the early-stage claim. The PR Newswire release dated Sept. 30, 2025 announces todo's launch of its shakes, so it is under 2 years old. Distribution is DTC only via drink-todo.com (shipping to the US and Canada), with no retail listed. The founder is named as Niket Soni, and nothing suggests a parent company. The independent search found no funding for this company. The CB Insights hit is Todo Verde, a different company, and the Tracxn hits are for other entities (a 2016 'Todo' and Todo Works), none matched to this brand. The '25,000+ customers' and 'As Seen On' claims are unverified, and the site's 50% clearance sale suggests some scale or inventory issues. That is not enough to contradict the small footprint, so the company fits as early-stage.
founders_supported_explanation: Niket Soni's claim holds up. The about-us and collection pages call 'Niket' Founder & CEO and give his Biomedical Science and Nutrition background and his struggle with low energy and digestive issues. The PR Newswire, Yahoo Finance and Medium pages tie the full name 'Niket Soni' to founding todo / Drink Todo. The Christine claim fails. Neither page cited for her mentions her. The collection page's 'Meet the founders' section is cut off after Niket, and the Boxing Day page has no mention of her. The only place she appears is the about-us page, which isn't cited for her. That page labels her 'Creative Director', not co-founder, and places her under 'the creative mastermind's story'. Her description there (storytelling, branding, passion for health, wellness and travel) matches the claim's background, but no cited source shows her as a founder of todo. Her 'Co-founder' role is therefore unsupported.

name: Short Story
early_stage_explanation: The agent's own sources show that Short Story (drinkshortstory.com) is a brand that launched in 2026. It is a family-founded electrolyte drink mix company sold direct-to-consumer and at local markets, including Denver's South Pearl Street Farmers Market. It has no retail distribution yet, only plans to expand. Nothing indicates it is owned by a larger company. The independent search results (PitchBook, Tracxn, Fortune, Caplight) are about a different, unrelated company: a San Francisco clothing subscription startup for petite women with YC and Tribe Capital backing. That is a name collision, so its $3M+ in funding does not apply here. No evidence shows outside funding for the electrolyte brand, so it fits the early-stage definition.
founders_supported_explanation: Claim 3 (Suzanne) failed. The Instagram page never mentions Suzanne or the phrase 'co-founder Suzanne', so the claim's main evidence is not in the source. The about page says only that Danielle is 'building Short Story alongside her husband Oliver and her sister-in-law Suzanne'. It never calls Suzanne a founder or co-founder, and its 'founders' photo caption names no one. Her founder status is therefore not shown. Claims 1 and 2 hold up. Danielle Nuss is listed as Co-Founder on LinkedIn, called 'co-founder' in the press release and 'co-founder Danielle' on the about page, and the pregnancy and home-made electrolyte origin story is confirmed. Oliver Nuss is listed as Co-Founder on LinkedIn, and the about page names Oliver as Danielle's husband building the company with her.
